requirements.invariant: Project category enablement and allocation is one conflict-aware complete-set operation preserving absent, enabled-without-allocation, explicit zero and positive Money; it therefore needs one set-level revision that also exists for an empty set.

The category-configuration revision is dedicated to the complete selected-category/allocation set. It is not the Project entity revision, any allocation-row revision, a maximum/sum/timestamp or LocalDataVersion/content hash; rename, details and archive cannot change it.

Every Project begins with category-configuration revision 1, including zero allocations. A future authoritative complete-set writer must lock the exact Project, compare the expected configuration revision, atomically replace the set, increment once only for a material change, and leave it unchanged for a semantic no-op.

A locally accepted new Project durably carries projected configuration revision 1 with its complete pending allocation set. That projection is not authoritative and this foundation does not reconcile or advance the revision before trusted readback.

Postgres stores the full integral UInt64 range losslessly as numeric; every Project Sync projection casts it to canonical decimal text and local SQLite stores text, preventing signed-64 or floating-point truncation across restart.

This provider-independent prerequisite adds no configuration command/provider/app/MCP behavior, changes no category visibility rule, does not resolve O-026 or A-003/A-004/A-015, and touches no Firebase, hosted, migration-source, production, release or cutover system.

verification.expected: Static proof binds the Core configuration revision only to the dedicated column and rejects Project/allocation/content-derived substitutes.
pgTAP proves exact numeric type/range/default/backfill, initial 1 for empty/nonempty configurations, invalid fractional/zero/overflow refusal and archive changing only Project revision.
The complete local target schema has no warning-level advisor findings.
An authenticated active member reads the added revision only through the unchanged visible Project row.
Anonymous, removed, foreign and nonmember readers gain no Project or revision visibility and no mutation privilege.
Both unchanged-authority Project streams cast the dedicated numeric revision to text and retain signed active-membership filters without a new stream.
A new pending Project atomically carries revision text 1 with its allocations through encrypted close/reopen, while local schema preserves maximum UInt64 text.
A failed/duplicate local Project acceptance cannot leave a Project revision row without its complete pending aggregate, and no local code synthesizes revision from child rows.
Preexisting synthetic target Projects backfill exactly to 1 and no Firebase/source field is consumed.
Server default 1, Sync text 1 and local pending text 1 agree without clearing pending allocations or claiming authoritative readback.

The exact implementation commit passes conversion controls, complete target tests, local Supabase tests, repeatable generation and both staging builds without Firebase, hosted, migration-source or production access.
